findings.title: Streaming on the default OpenAI adapter (and Gemini/Vertex, LangChain Ollama) bypasses the provider guard; the declared cancel capability is not backed by those stream paths
findings.evidence: openai_responses_adapter.py:676 and :778, gemini_adapter.py:218/:248/:412 and ollama_adapter.py:391 wrap the SDK stream only in `_provider_dependency_attempt()`. The other streaming adapters (openai chat/compat/azure, claude, mistral, cohere, bedrock, native ollama) go through `BaseLLMAdapter._execute_streaming`, which runs `assert_protected_provider_call_allowed()`, the deadline check, `check_llm_tenant_quota`, rate limit / circuit breaker / retry, the external-operation attempt and `stream_with_external_operation_lifecycle` (the stream-transport registration used by the cancel seam). Probe `probe_stream_guard.py` (guard patched to deny): `OpenAIChatResponsesAdapter.generate_messages` denied, `stream_messages` ALLOWED, `OpenAIChatCompletionsAdapter.stream_messages` denied. The registry declares OPENAI/GEMINI/VERTEX_GEMINI as `terminated` and OLLAMA as `transport_closed` (registrations/external_operation_seams.py), but those stream paths never register a transport. The R011 test `test_declared_cancel_capability_equals_observed_outcome` registers a stream into the seam by hand, so it cannot see this: mutant M12 (remove the `stream_registry.register(...)` call in provider_stream_admission.py) SURVIVES all 150 D3 tests. The docstring of `contracts/llm_adapter.py` and HARNESS-02 `H02-llm-provider-boundary` state that every physical provider access runs the guard.
findings.impact: For the default `openai` provider (registered adapter = OpenAIChatResponsesAdapter) a streamed call is not subject to the protected-work/deadline guard, the tenant token quota, rate limiting, circuit breaker or retry, and cannot be cancelled through the registered seam although the registry declares `terminated`. Mitigation observed: no in-tree runtime caller of `stream_messages`/`stream_with_tools` exists (grep over intergrax/, agents/, applications/ finds only wrappers), so the defect is latent until a streaming consumer is wired.
findings.reproduction: uv run python docs/project/maintainers/qualification/iiac_evidence/PDC-X/D3/adversarial_scripts/probe_stream_guard.py ; mutant M12 via adversarial_scripts/run_mutants.py M12
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Route the stream paths of openai_responses_adapter, gemini_adapter and ollama_adapter through `_execute_streaming` (same admission, quota, resilience and transport registration as the other adapters); add a test that drives each shipped adapter's real `stream_messages` with a fake SDK and asserts (a) the guard is consulted and (b) the stream transport is registered with the provider seam, and a source gate that forbids an adapter stream method that calls the SDK outside `_execute_streaming`.

findings.title: Refusal / content-filter normalization holds only for a subset of provider paths; every streaming path and several buffered paths report COMPLETED with empty content
findings.evidence: `build_adapter_response` normalizes whatever it is given, but most provider paths never pass a finish reason or refusal to it: OpenAI chat `stream_messages` (openai_chat_completions_adapter.py:128-175) ignores `delta.refusal` and `finish_reason`; the plain `generate_messages`/`stream_messages` of gemini (:158, :230, :262), cohere (:133, :189), bedrock converse/invoke (:515, :551, :614, :662), LangChain Ollama (:346, :403, :421) and the streams of mistral, openai-responses, claude and native ollama build the final response with the default finish reason. Probe `probe_refusal_stream.py`: a stream carrying `delta.refusal` and a stream ending `finish_reason=content_filter` both end as `finish=COMPLETED refusal=None content=''`. The R009 tests exercise `parse_finish_reason`, `build_adapter_response` and the OpenAI/Claude non-stream mappers directly, not the provider stream paths; the `SAFETY`/`guardrail_intervened`/`ERROR_TOXIC` vocabulary of `parse_finish_reason` has no producer on the Gemini, Bedrock and Cohere plain paths.
findings.impact: A refused or filtered streamed answer is indistinguishable from an empty successful answer; downstream governance keyed on REFUSAL/CONTENT_FILTER never fires on streams.
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Read the provider stop/finish/refusal signal in every stream and plain-generate path and feed it to `build_adapter_response`; extend the R009 tests to drive each shipped adapter's stream and plain paths with a fake SDK refusal and content-filter payload.

findings.title: `LLMCallConfig.timeout_sec` is never enforced or forwarded to the SDK call
findings.evidence: `BaseLLMAdapter._execute` / `_execute_streaming` (base_llm_adapter.py:275-345) compute `effective_timeout` and only reject a budget that is already <= 0; `timeout_sec` is then carried in `effective_config`, which `call_with_retry` and `execute_with_resilience` do not read (retry.py uses max_retries/retry_on_status/backoff only; resilience.py has no timeout). No provider adapter passes a timeout to its SDK call. Probe `probe_timeout.py`: `OpenAIChatCompletionsAdapter(timeout_sec=0.1, max_retries=0)` with an SDK call that sleeps 1.0 s returned 'late' after 1.06 s and the SDK kwargs contain no timeout. No unit test in tests/unit/llm_adapters or the D3 suite exercises `timeout_sec`.
findings.impact: A configured per-call timeout is a dead setting: a hung provider call is bounded only by the SDK default or an outer execution deadline that is consulted at admission.
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Apply the effective timeout to the SDK request (per-call `timeout=` kwarg or client option) in `_execute`/`_execute_streaming` and add a test with a slow fake SDK; or remove `timeout_sec` from the contract and record the exclusion.

findings.title: The pre-call capability check has no production feature source; the XD-01 gate is satisfiable by a dormant caller (carries F-37)
findings.evidence: `LLMAdapterRegistry.require_capabilities` is called in production only by `_require_llm_features` in intergrax/applications/_shared/llm_resolver.py:300, and `required_llm_features` has no caller outside tests (grep `required_llm_features=` over intergrax/, agents/, applications/: none; `llm_profile_source=`: none). The runtime resolver `intergrax/runtime/wiring/llm_resolver.py:166` (used by XD-01 itself) has no such parameter. `test_xd01_required_model_capabilities_are_checked_at_composition_time` only asserts that some production file calls `require_capabilities`, which the dormant `_require_llm_features` satisfies. The adapter-level raise in `BaseLLMAdapter.stream_with_tools` (before provider I/O) is the real fail-closed backstop and holds. Mutant M03 (failover falls back to `adapters[0]` when no chain member declares the feature) SURVIVES because the base class raises anyway; an under-reporting third-party member would stream undeclared.
findings.impact: `AgentContract.required_llm_features` is accepted and normalized but never reaches adapter resolution at runtime, so the ADR-PDC-03 statement that the runtime checks requested features before the call is true only for the adapter methods themselves.
findings.reproduction: grep -rn "required_llm_features=" intergrax agents applications ; mutant M03 via adversarial_scripts/run_mutants.py M03
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Pass the agent contract's `required_llm_features` into the resolver on the runtime composition path (both resolvers), make XD-01 drive that path, and pin the failover pre-check with a test using `UnderReportingStreamAdapter` (declared False, streams anyway).

findings.title: The `llm_adapters` unit suites cited as closure evidence are not green at the audited SHA
findings.evidence: `uv run --extra <all llm extras> pytest tests/unit/llm_adapters tests/qualification/ce_02 tests/qualification/pdc_x/d3`: 12 failed / 692 passed / 8 skipped. Eight failures are deterministic and also red at the control checkout 35b6772af~1 (13 failed there, one of them fixed since): 4 x `test_fixture_strict_adapter_parity` (platform_proofs `IncidentInvestigatorAgent` cannot be instantiated: abstract `run`), 3 x `test_ollama_tool_calling::test_unsupported_tool_choice_rejects_before_provider` (regex stale since d5f5cde99; the message now ends 'or a forced function choice'), 1 x `test_registry_model_contract::test_invalid_adapter_missing_model_fails_clearly` (the registry raises TypeError from the Protocol isinstance check before the documented `LLMAdapterRegistrationError`; the AttributeError branch of `_resolve_adapter_model_id` is unreachable through `create`). 4 further tests (`test_missing_optional_llm_dependency_is_controlled`, 3 x `test_provider_creation_surfaces_dependency_error_without_sdk`) fail only in the combined run with the SDK extras installed (state dependent) and pass in isolation (28 passed). In the default environment (no extras) `test_adapter_conformance.py` and `test_structured_output_flags.py` fail at collection (`import anthropic`).
findings.impact: R001, R007, R008, R010, R012, R013 and R017 name 'llm_adapters unit suites' as requalification evidence; a green replay cannot be claimed, and two stale tests encode a contract (error type, message) that differs from the product.
findings.reproduction: uv run --extra llm-anthropic --extra llm-mistral --extra llm-ollama --extra llm-langchain-ollama --extra llm-gemini --extra llm-bedrock --extra llm-cohere-native --extra llm-openai pytest tests/unit/llm_adapters tests/qualification/ce_02 tests/qualification/pdc_x/d3 -q -p no:randomly
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Repair or retire the stale tests (regex, protocol order, fixture agent `run`), guard the two extra-dependent modules with `importorskip`, and isolate the registry-state tests; then record a green replay.
findings.owner_path: tests/unit/llm_adapters/ (test_ollama_tool_calling.py, test_registry_model_contract.py, test_fixture_strict_adapter_parity.py, test_adapter_conformance.py, test_structured_output_flags.py, test_llm_provider_registry.py, test_p2_002_c_provider_registration.py); platform_proofs/scenarios/ai_incident_investigation/

findings.title: The TENANT-X replay gate cited for R018 is red: carrier count 831 vs 819
findings.evidence: `uv run --extra integrations-duckdb pytest tests/qualification/tenant_x`: 1 failed / 193 passed. `test_tenant_x_p0_current_head.py::test_tx_p0_r3_head_q02_class_field_carrier_count_stable` asserts 831 == 819 (`TENANT_X_REPLAY_HEAD_CARRIER_TOTAL`); the same test is green at the control checkout 35b6772af~1. findings.title: No typed provider-error taxonomy: retry and failover classify by `status_code` and class-name substrings
findings.evidence: The row claims 'typed provider errors'. `intergrax/llm_adapters` defines no normalized provider error classes (auth, rate limit, timeout, invalid request, content filter, server); SDK exceptions propagate raw. `_is_retryable` (_shared/retry.py:81-99) decides by the `status_code` attribute and `any(token in type(exc).__name__.lower() for token in ('timeout','connection','rate','overloaded'))`. Probe `probe_failover.py` with the default failover policy: an exception class named `GenerateContentError` (a non-transient 400-style error) and one named `SeparateTenantError` both fail over and the same request reaches the secondary provider; status 401 stops; `CooperativeCancellationAbort` and `KeyboardInterrupt` stop (positive). Streaming calls have no failover at all (`FailoverLLMAdapter.stream_messages`/`stream_with_tools` pick the first declaring member and delegate).
findings.impact: Whether a request and its content are re-sent to another provider depends on a substring of a vendor class name; the taxonomy the matrix claims does not exist as a contract.
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Introduce a small typed provider-error contract mapped at the adapter boundary (or classify by an explicit allowlist of SDK types and status codes) and test it per provider with fake SDK errors.

findings.title: LangChain Ollama `stream_messages` silently re-issues the model call after a mid-stream failure
findings.evidence: ollama_adapter.py:413 `except Exception:` after partial output falls back to `self.chat.invoke(...)` and emits the whole answer again. Probe `probe_ollama_stream.py`: partials 'par','tial' then a ConnectionError yield a partial 'FULL REISSUED ANSWER' and a FINAL containing only the second answer; `invoke` is called once and the original error is swallowed. `NativeOllamaAdapter` (the registered `ollama` provider) is correct (`if emitted_partial: raise`).
findings.impact: Duplicated output and a second provider call after a transport close or failure; reachable only by constructing `LangChainOllamaAdapter` directly (it is not the registered default).
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Re-raise when any partial was emitted (as the native adapter does) and add a test.

findings.title: The VBN classification of provider defaults named as R019's test case is not present
findings.evidence: The matrix test case is 'VBN register classification of each default' (provider `DEFAULT_MODEL` constants, `LLMProfile.lab`, rag default embedding provider). `LLMProfile.lab()` (llm_profile.py:108, Ollama `llama3.1:latest`) is consumed by intergrax/applications/contracts/environment_profile/bundles.py:243 and presets.py:138; provider `DEFAULT_MODEL` constants are floating aliases (`claude-3-5-sonnet-latest`, `mistral-large-latest`, `llama3.1:latest`, `gemini-2.5-flash`, `gpt-5-mini`). No EBH-6 register row, test or VBN document names them (grep over tests/qualification and docs/project/maintainers/qualification finds none), and the EBH-6 class gates skip `/providers/` trees (`_aj_class_gate_scan.py:221`). `tests/qualification/ebh_6` is green, which does not cover these defaults.
findings.impact: R019 closure cannot be shown from the named register; the defaults may well be allowed (vendor-owned tree, lab preset) but are unclassified.
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Add a classification row (allowed vendor-owned default / lab-only) per default to the register and a test that fails when a new default is added unclassified.

findings.title: Runtime attribution records the requested model id, never the model the provider reports serving
findings.evidence: `adapter_response_from_openai_chat_completion` takes `model=` from the adapter and ignores `res.model` (the probe SDK reports 'm', the adapter model is 'gpt-4o-mini', the response model is 'gpt-4o-mini'); only `system_fingerprint` is kept (openai_completion_mapping.py:150-160). `LLMAdapterResponse` has no served-model field. The pin is a model string, and the shipped defaults are floating aliases (F-D3-09).
findings.impact: Attribution (FRZ-TRC-04) cannot show which snapshot answered when an alias is pinned.
findings.reproduction: read intergrax/llm_adapters/_shared/openai_completion_mapping.py:140-186; adversarial_scripts/probe_timeout.py builds a ChatCompletion whose model differs from the adapter model
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Add an optional served-model field to the response / provider extensions and fill it from each provider's response where one is reported.

findings.title: `model_catalog.yaml` carries a duplicate record and the loader accepts duplicates and non-positive windows
findings.evidence: `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct` appears twice (model_catalog.yaml:256 and :284, different `provider_hints`); `ModelCatalog.from_mapping` appends every row and `lookup_exact` returns the first, `_merge` de-duplicates only overlays; `int(row['context_window_tokens'])` is not validated as positive. The R023 'single source' tests do not check catalog uniqueness.
findings.impact: Latent: a later edit of one duplicate with a different window would silently be ignored (first wins).
findings.reproduction: python -c "import yaml,collections;d=yaml.safe_load(open('intergrax/llm_adapters/registry/model_catalog.yaml'));print([k for k,v in collections.Counter(m['model_id'] for m in d['models']).items() if v>1])"
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Reject duplicate ids and non-positive windows in `from_mapping`, add a catalog integrity test and merge the two rows.

findings.title: Tenant token quota is one process-wide cap that silently disables itself on a malformed value
findings.evidence: quota.py `_max_tokens_per_tenant` returns 0 (disabled) on `ValueError`, uses a single `INTERGRAX_LLM_TENANT_MAX_TOKENS` for every tenant and counts in-process metrics only (`get_llm_metrics_collector().tenant_total_tokens`).
findings.impact: A typo in the cap turns the control off without a signal; the cap is not per-tenant configuration; counters reset per process.
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Fail closed (raise) on a malformed non-empty value; document the per-process scope or move the counter behind the tenant store.

findings.title: Test strength gaps in the D3 gates (2 of 14 mutants survive; the AST gate accepts any call)
findings.evidence: Mutation sample (run_mutants.py, scratch worktree at the audited SHA, control green 176 passed / 5 skipped): 12 killed, 2 survived: M03 (failover fallback to `adapters[0]`, see F-D3-04) and M12 (stream registration removed, see F-D3-01). `test_every_provider_source_class_declares_what_it_implements` treats any `return <call>` as a declaration (`_declares_true`), so `return bool(self._x)` passes; it is the only gate for gemini, mistral and cohere because their SDKs are not installed in the default environment.
findings.impact: Regressions of the two surviving mutants would not be caught by the D3 suite.
findings.reproduction: python docs/project/maintainers/qualification/iiac_evidence/PDC-X/D3/adversarial_scripts/run_mutants.py (adapt WT/OUT paths); results in logs/mutation/
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Add the two missing tests (F-D3-01, F-D3-04) and tighten `_declares_true` to constant True or delegation to a named flag.

findings.title: Positive: F-49 and F-50 are resolved; the shared-slug defect class is closed; EBH-5 is green

Mutants M10 (dispatch inverted) and M11 (`enabled` hard-wired) of openai/register.py are killed by p6_ecapfix. `tests/qualification/pdc_x/{p6_ecapfix,reg_p,p6_model,p6_impact}`: 110 passed. `tests/qualification/ebh_5`: 243 passed with the `integrations-duckdb` extra.

findings.title: Environment notes and known reds
findings.evidence: The default environment lacks the optional extras: 5 D3 tests skip (`importorskip`), 4 ebh_5 tests fail without `duckdb` (243 pass with the extra), 2 unit modules error at collection without `anthropic`. The pdc_x/xd (80 passed), d3 and p6 runs exited normally: debt R-05 (pytest not exiting after the summary) was not reproduced. findings.title: Documentation drift: the architecture and plan docs do not describe the declared-capability contract; the B-D3 commits carry an AI co-author trailer that predates the repo rule
findings.evidence: `LLMFeature`, `CancelCapability`, `supports_tool_streaming` and `LLMCapabilityMismatchError` appear only in ADR_PDC_03 (still headed 'Decision (proposed)'), not in docs/project/architecture/LLM_ADAPTERS.md or its plan. Commits 35b6772af and ff469148d carry a `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer; the no-attribution rule was added 2026-11-13 (68632a06f), after those commits (2026-11-12), so no violation is recorded.
findings.impact: Maintainers learn the contract only from the ADR.
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Add a short section to LLM_ADAPTERS.md and its plan in the D3 doc lane.
